ev.q: CDC analyzed data from the 2004 National Immunization Survey (NIS).
The results indicated that 71.5% of white and 50.1% of black children ( Table 1 ) were ever breastfed.
Weighted percentages were calculated using statistical software to account for complex sample design.
71.5% of non-Hispanic white children were ever breastfed compared with 50.1% of non-Hispanic black children
Breastfeeding rates were lower among black than white children within every subgroup studied
Within each income group, the proportion of black children who were ever breastfed was 10 to 17 percentage points lower
The NIS uses random-digit dialing to survey households with children aged 19--35 months
